documents.title: Optional Syllabus Statements for the Acceptable or Unacceptable Use of AI Tools in Your Course
documents.summary: A set of four optional sample syllabus statements from the Academic Senate, from broad permission to a full ban, that instructors adapt and fill in with a penalty. It also tells instructors to be specific about permitted activities and to think about penalties. It sets no campus-wide rule itself.
documents.stance_why: The document offers four template statements for instructors to adjust ('Please adjust the statement to reflect your parameters'), spanning 'You are welcome to use generative AI tools' to 'is not permitted in this class'. It sets no single rule and hands the choice to instructors, so delegates with the templates listed as tiers.

units.why: The sample statements are offered for instructors to 'adjust ... to reflect your parameters and to fit your course', so the rule is set per course by the instructor; P04 fits better than P09 because the point is who decides, not that a statement is mandatory.
units.anchor: Please adjust the statement to reflect your parameters

units.why: Instructors are told to 'Be specific and let students know what class activities are permitted and not permitted', i.e. to state AI expectations in the class policy; this is P09 addressed to instructors.
units.anchor: Be specific and let students know what class activities are permitted

units.why: Instructors who prohibit AI are told to 'think about the appropriate level of penalty for first-time offenders and those who repeatedly violate'; this concerns setting penalties in advance, so P37.
units.anchor: think about the appropriate level of penalty for first-time offenders

units.why: Sample statement 1 says 'You are welcome to use generative AI tools' in the class, a broad default permission; coded as a template option (P02), addressed to students.
units.anchor: You are welcome to use generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Dall-e, etc.) in this class.

units.why: The template makes students 'responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query' (no IP violation, misinformation or unethical content); ownership of what is submitted is P29, with the content conditions kept in the policy text.
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query
units.policy: Students are responsible for the information they submit based on an AI query, for instance that it does not violate intellectual property laws, contain misinformation, or unethical content.

units.why: The broad-permission template states 'Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited', a disclosure rule for students (P24, no tool or prompt details named).
units.anchor: Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited

units.why: The template has a placeholder '[insert the penalty here*]' for unauthorized AI use, so it prescribes that a penalty be stated in advance (P37).
units.anchor: Any assignment that is found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways

units.why: 'When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification' tells unsure students to ask the instructor: P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification.

units.why: Template 2 permits AI 'only for the following activities' (brainstorming and refining ideas, research questions, finding information, outlines), a narrow list of permitted uses; P15 is chosen because brainstorming leads the list, and the 'only' makes the unit_stance restrict.
units.anchor: is permitted in this course only for the following activities
units.policy: Use of generative AI tools is permitted only for brainstorming and refining ideas, fine tuning research questions, finding information on the topic, drafting an outline, and checking grammar and style.

units.why: 'Checking grammar and style' is a listed permitted use of AI for prose, separate from code, so P18.
units.anchor: Checking grammar and style.

units.why: Template 3 states AI use 'is not permitted in this class', a full ban for the course: P01.
units.anchor: is not permitted in this class

units.why: The full-ban template says AI use 'may be considered a violation of CSULB's Policy on Academic Integrity Regarding Cheating and Plagiarism, since the work is not your own', classing it as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: may be considered a violation of
units.policy: Any use of AI tools for work in the class may be considered a violation of CSULB's Policy on Academic Integrity Regarding Cheating and Plagiarism, since the work is not the student's own.

units.why: 'will result in [insert the penalty here*]' is a penalty clause for the full-ban template; P37 because it states consequences in advance.
units.anchor: The use of any AI tools will result in [insert the penalty here*].

units.why: The partial-ban template forbids AI 'Impersonating you in classroom contexts', e.g. discussion board prompts and Zoom chat content; these are students' own course communications, so P58 fits best.
units.anchor: Impersonating you in classroom contexts
units.policy: Using generative AI tools to impersonate the student in classroom contexts, such as composing discussion board prompts assigned to them or content put into a Zoom chat, is not permitted.

units.why: Partial-ban item: AI may not be used for 'Completing group work that your group has assigned to you, unless it is mutually agreed'; the AI would produce work submitted as the student's own contribution, so P19.
units.anchor: Completing group work that your group has assigned to you
units.policy: Using generative AI tools to complete group work assigned to the student by their group is not permitted unless it is mutually agreed that the tool may be used.

units.why: Partial-ban item forbids AI 'Writing a draft of a writing assignment', so AI produces work that gets submitted: P19.
units.anchor: Writing a draft of a writing assignment

units.why: Partial-ban item forbids AI 'Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments': AI produces the submitted text, P19.
units.anchor: Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments

documents.title: AI Guidelines
documents.summary: The Division of IT's campus guidelines define terms, sort general uses into allowed, restricted and prohibited, and recommend four course policy levels. Students follow each instructor's rule; data, vendor and research rules are also set. Violations fall under existing conduct policies.
documents.stance_why: Faculty are 'recommended to select one of the following course policy levels' (Prohibited, Limited, Permitted with Disclosure, Integrated) and students must 'Follow the instructor's requirements', so the document hands course decisions to instructors and lists tiers; the general allowed/restricted/prohibited list covers non-course uses.

units.why: The preamble says CSULB 'supports the responsible and ethical use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies for enhancing teaching, learning, research, and campus services', an institution-level framing statement: P56.
units.anchor: supports the responsible and ethical use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies

units.why: Scope statement: the guidelines 'apply to all members of the CSULB community' for academic, research, administrative and creative purposes; scope belongs with the framework (P56) since definitions are coded separately as P61.
units.anchor: These guidelines apply to all members of the CSULB community

units.why: Defines Generative AI as 'Tools that produce text, images, audio, video, code ...', fixing what the guidelines cover: P61.
units.anchor: Tools that produce text, images, audio, video, code, or any other artifacts or content
units.policy: Generative AI (GenAI) means tools that produce text, images, audio, video, code, or any other artifacts or content.

units.why: Defines 'Sensitive Data' as information protected by FERPA, HIPAA, IRB protocols, CSULB policies or CSU regulations, setting the scope of the data rules: P61.
units.anchor: Information protected by FERPA, HIPAA, IRB protocols, CSULB policies, or CSU regulations
units.policy: Sensitive Data means information protected by FERPA, HIPAA, IRB protocols, CSULB policies, or CSU regulations.

units.why: Defines 'Disclosure' as 'A clear statement identifying how and when AI tools were used'; a definition, so P61 rather than the P24 requirement itself.
units.anchor: A clear statement identifying how and when AI tools were used
units.policy: Disclosure means a clear statement identifying how and when AI tools were used.

units.why: Faculty recommendation: 'Define course-level expectations for AI, using sample syllabus language'; a call to state expectations per course (P09).
units.anchor: Define course-level expectations for AI, using sample syllabus language provided by CSULB.

units.why: Students are told to 'Follow the instructor's requirements regarding the use of AI', which places the decision with the instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Follow the instructor's requirements regarding the use of AI.

units.why: When AI is permitted students must 'disclose the use of AI ... by citing use of AI resources': a disclosure-with-submission rule, P24.
units.anchor: If the instructor permits the use of AI, disclose the use of AI
units.policy: If the instructor permits the use of AI, students disclose the use of AI and maintain integrity in all submissions by citing use of AI resources.

units.why: A conditional ban that follows the instructor's decision ('If the instructor does not permit ... do not use AI'); coded P04 (instructor decides) not P01, because the university sets no default ban.
units.anchor: does not permit the use of AI in their classes, do not use AI

units.why: Staff must 'Consult the appropriate administrator or supervisor before using AI', a rule on staff use of AI in their own work: P59.
units.anchor: Consult the appropriate administrator or supervisor before using AI.

units.why: Approved staff AI use must ensure 'compliance with data and security protocols': data protection (P50).
units.anchor: ensuring compliance with data and security protocols
units.policy: If approved, staff use AI responsibly to support operations, ensuring compliance with data and security protocols.

units.why: Listed under 'Allowed (with human oversight and disclosure)': brainstorming and outlining are permitted general uses (P15).
units.anchor: Brainstorming and outlining
units.policy: Brainstorming and outlining are allowed with human oversight and disclosure.

units.why: Under 'Allowed (with human oversight and disclosure)': grammar, translation and accessibility support with verification; prose-support uses: P18.
units.anchor: Grammar, translation, and accessibility support (with verification)
units.policy: Grammar, translation, and accessibility support are allowed with human oversight, disclosure and verification.

units.why: Allowed use 'Administrative efficiency (e.g., summarization, scheduling)' concerns staff and faculty operational work, so P59.
units.anchor: Administrative efficiency (e.g., summarization, scheduling)
units.policy: Administrative efficiency (e.g., summarization, scheduling) is allowed with human oversight and disclosure.

units.why: Listed as 'Restricted (requires approval/secure tools)': handling sensitive data with AI needs approval, a data-protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: Handling of sensitive data (FERPA/PII/PHI, research data)
units.policy: Handling of sensitive data (FERPA/PII/PHI, research data) with AI is restricted and requires approval or secure tools.

units.why: Under 'Restricted': automated decisions including grading 'must include human review'; P46 (humans assign grades) is the closest type for the grading part.
units.anchor: Automated decision-making in admissions, grading, HR, or financial processes (must include human review)
units.policy: Automated decision-making in admissions, grading, HR, or financial processes is restricted and must include human review.

units.why: Listed under 'Prohibited': uploading sensitive data to unapproved tools; a data-protection prohibition (P50, not P49 because it is not course materials).
units.anchor: Uploading University sensitive data to unapproved AI tools

units.why: Listed under 'Prohibited'. It bans fabricating or falsifying data, citations or sources, a research-integrity rule; no type covers fabrication (P31 is about verifying output, P36 about classifying misconduct).
units.anchor: Fabricating or falsifying data, citations, or sources
units.uncovered_note: Prohibits fabricating or falsifying data, citations, or sources (with AI).

units.why: Under 'Prohibited': 'Misrepresenting AI-generated work as entirely one's own when prohibited'; submitted work must be the person's own: P29.
units.anchor: Misrepresenting AI-generated work as entirely one's own when prohibited

units.why: Under 'Prohibited': using AI to create harmful, discriminatory or illegal content; an ethics and harms rule, so P53.
units.anchor: Using AI to create harmful, discriminatory, or illegal content

units.why: 'Faculty should clearly define their AI usage policy in each course syllabus' is the syllabus-statement rule: P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly define their AI usage policy in each course syllabus.

units.why: Detection tools 'should not be used as sole evidence of misconduct': a limit on relying on detectors, P39.
units.anchor: should not be used as sole evidence of misconduct.

units.why: Faculty are recommended to pick from four named policy levels (Prohibited, Limited, Permitted with Disclosure, Integrated): P05 (named tiers).
units.anchor: Faculty are recommended to select one of the following course policy levels

units.why: Tier 'Prohibited' defined as 'AI use is not allowed in coursework'; a named level, P05.
units.anchor: AI use is not allowed in coursework.

units.why: Tier 'Limited': only specific uses such as formatting or grammar checking, with citation; a named level, P05.
units.anchor: Only specific uses (e.g., formatting, grammar checking etc.) are allowed with proper citation.

units.why: Tier 'Permitted with Disclosure': AI may draft or summarize with citation; named level, P05.
units.anchor: AI can be used for drafting/summarization with proper citation.

units.why: Tier 'Integrated': 'AI is required and embedded into assignments'; named level, P05 (the requirement is the tier's definition).
units.anchor: AI is required and embedded into assignments.

units.why: Students must 'Consult with their instructor about usage of AI in each class'; ask-first rule, P10 (each-class scope is incidental).
units.anchor: Consult with their instructor about usage of AI in each class.

units.why: If AI is permitted students must 'disclose tool name, purpose, and scope of AI use', specific details of the disclosure: P25.
units.anchor: disclose tool name, purpose, and scope of AI use
units.policy: If using AI is permitted, students disclose tool name, purpose, and scope of AI use.

units.why: Students must 'Carefully review AI content, verify accuracy': verification of AI output (P31), chosen over P24 because the verification duty is the main clause.
units.anchor: Carefully review AI content, verify accuracy, and provide citations
units.policy: Students carefully review AI content, verify accuracy, and provide citations and references where required.

units.why: Students must review AI content for bias and inaccuracies, which is critical evaluation of output: P31.
units.anchor: Review AI generated content for bias, inaccuracies, favoritism, prejudice, and discriminatory outcomes.

units.why: For research and creative activity, 'Use only Microsoft CoPilot and ChatGPT provided by CSULB' with guardrails; vetted-tool rule, P50.
units.anchor: Use only Microsoft CoPilot and ChatGPT provided by CSULB

units.why: Research rule 'Follow IRB and sponsor guidelines' defers to IRB and sponsor rules: P62.
units.anchor: Follow IRB and sponsor guidelines.

units.why: Research rule: 'Do not upload restricted data/code to consumer AI platforms'; data protection (P50) rather than P20, which is about student assignment code.
units.anchor: Do not upload restricted data/code to consumer AI platforms.

units.why: Research rule on attributing AI contributions in publications, i.e. scholarship (P62).
units.anchor: Attribute AI contributions in publications per disciplinary standards.

units.why: Research rule to 'Document model versions, prompts, and limitations when relevant', naming model and prompt details: P25.
units.anchor: Document model versions, prompts, and limitations when relevant to reproducibility.

units.why: The privacy section says 'Use campus-approved AI platforms when available' and 'use only Microsoft Copilot, and ChatGPT provided by CSULB' via SSO; a university-provided sanctioned tool as the allowed option, P17.
units.anchor: use only Microsoft Copilot, and ChatGPT provided by CSULB
units.policy: Use campus-approved AI platforms when available; use only Microsoft Copilot and ChatGPT provided by CSULB through Single Sign On.

units.why: 'Apply data minimization and anonymization where possible' protects personal data: P50.
units.anchor: Apply data minimization and anonymization where possible.

units.why: Requires reporting suspected data breaches to DOIT; closest type is data protection (P50).
units.anchor: Report suspected data breaches to CSULB DOIT immediately.

units.why: AI-generated accessibility content must be reviewed for accuracy: verify output, P31.
units.anchor: Ensure AI-generated content (captions, transcripts, alt text) is reviewed for accuracy.

units.why: Avoid tools that are not ADA compliant: an access and equity rule, P51.
units.anchor: Avoid reliance on tools that are not ADA compliant.

units.why: Universal design for AI-supported materials is an access rule: P51.
units.anchor: Apply universal design principles to all AI-supported materials.

units.why: 'Use CSU/CSULB procurement processes for new AI tools' is institutional review of AI vendors: P65.
units.anchor: Use CSU/CSULB procurement processes for new AI tools.

units.why: Evaluation of vendors' privacy, accessibility and security compliance (VPAT, SOC2, FERPA/HIPAA): P65.
units.anchor: Evaluate privacy, accessibility, and security compliance

units.why: Prefer vendors that are transparent about data usage: vendor review, P65.
units.anchor: Prefer vendors offering transparency on data usage and storage.

units.why: States that ATS offers workshops, consultations and resources to students, faculty and staff; support for learning about AI (P63).
units.anchor: Workshops, consultations, and resources are offered by ATS

units.why: Students who do not conform are 'Subject to University policies, including those regarding student conduct', routing violations into conduct processes: P36.
units.anchor: Subject to University policies, including those regarding student conduct.

units.why: Faculty and staff nonconformity is 'Subject to relevant University policies'; this is an enforcement statement for employees that no type covers (P36 is about student misconduct).
units.anchor: Subject to relevant University policies.
units.uncovered_note: Faculty/staff who do not follow the AI guidelines are subject to relevant University policies.

units.why: The AI Steering Committee 'Oversees campus-wide AI guidelines', stating who maintains the framework: P56.
units.anchor: Oversees campus-wide AI guidelines

documents.title: Student Guidelines on Generative AI
documents.summary: A student-facing page explaining that instructors may allow broad, specific or no AI use, and that students must check the syllabus and ask before using AI. It requires citation of permitted use, warns of discipline for unauthorized use, and notes AI features in ordinary software count. It raises equity and sustainability concerns.
documents.stance_why: Although instructors decide per course, the page's operative rule is 'DO NOT use GenAI unless you have received an OK from your instructor', so AI is banned unless explicitly permitted: restrict rather than delegates, since the student-facing default is no AI without permission.

units.why: Names that some systems draw on creative work, use substantial energy and reflect training-data bias, tied to CSULB's equity and sustainability commitments: P53.
units.anchor: Some systems draw from existing creative work, require substantial energy to operate

units.why: 'AI is most effective when it supports learning and growth rather than replacing the effort required to attain deeper insights' is a learning rationale: P41.
units.anchor: AI is most effective when it supports learning and growth rather than replacing the effort

units.why: Because 'Instructors' expectations can vary by course', students 'must communicate with them' before using AI; ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: students must communicate with them to understanding how AI may be used appropriately
units.policy: Instructors' expectations can vary by course, so students must communicate with the instructor to understand how AI may be used appropriately before using it for coursework.

units.why: Where the instructor allows broad use, 'your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited': P24.
units.anchor: your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited

units.why: Permitted AI use must follow the Policy on Academic Integrity Regarding Cheating and Plagiarism, putting AI use under the integrity process: P36.
units.anchor: must follow CSULB's Policy on Academic Integrity Regarding Cheating and Plagiarism
units.policy: Permitted AI use must follow CSULB's Policy on Academic Integrity Regarding Cheating and Plagiarism.

units.why: Unauthorized use 'may result in academic disciplining, and a lower, or failing grade'; consequences named in advance, P37.
units.anchor: may result in academic disciplining, and a lower, or failing grade

units.why: 'If you have any doubt about an assignment, or deliverable, be sure to seek clarification and guidance from your instructor': P10.
units.anchor: be sure to seek clarification and guidance from your instructor

units.why: Example of specific permitted use: brainstorming and refining ideas and research questions, finding information, outlines, grammar checking; brainstorming leads the list so P15.
units.anchor: your instructor may allow usage of generative AI tools for brainstorming
units.policy: An instructor may allow generative AI tools for brainstorming, refining ideas and research questions, finding information, drafting an outline, or checking grammar and style.

units.why: States the guidelines also cover 'AI features built into existing software packages (e.g. Microsoft Copilot)': P07.
units.anchor: This also includes AI features built into existing software packages (e.g. Microsoft Copilot).

units.why: 'seek clear guidance from your instructor BEFORE you use generative AI in your coursework': ask first, P10.
units.anchor: Make sure to seek clear guidance from your instructor BEFORE you use generative AI

units.why: An instructor 'may fully prohibit the usage of GenAI', forbidding partial and specific use too; the instructor decides, so P04.
units.anchor: your instructor may fully prohibit the usage of GenAI
units.policy: An instructor may fully prohibit the usage of GenAI, which also forbids students from partial or specific usage for assignments and coursework.

units.why: When AI is forbidden, examples include using it 'to compose discussion posts, or create content for Zoom chats': students' course communications, P58.
units.anchor: to compose discussion posts, or create content for Zoom chats
units.policy: Where GenAI is forbidden, students may not use it to compose discussion posts or create content for Zoom chats.

units.why: Under a prohibition students may not use AI for 'writing assignment drafts, or writing full and or partial sentences and paragraphs', i.e. AI producing submitted work: P19.
units.anchor: writing full and or partial sentences and paragraphs for class assignments and submissions
units.policy: Where GenAI is forbidden, students may not use it for completing group work, writing assignment drafts, or writing full or partial sentences and paragraphs for class assignments and submissions.

units.why: 'DO NOT use GenAI unless you have received an OK from your instructor' sets a fallback: no AI without instructor permission: P06.
units.anchor: use GenAI unless you have received an OK from your instructor

units.why: Even if allowed, contributions 'must be cited. If they are not, it may still be considered plagiarism': failure to disclose is itself a violation, P28.
units.anchor: If they are not, it may still be considered plagiarism.
units.policy: Even where an instructor allows AI-generated work, the contributions must be cited; if they are not, it may still be considered plagiarism.

units.why: Notes GenAI 'is a rapidly evolving topic, and this document will be updated based on any changes in technology, and University policies': P54.
units.anchor: this document will be updated based on any changes in technology

documents.title: AI for Teaching and Learning
documents.summary: A faculty-facing page that presents benefits of AI (tutoring, feedback, accessibility), concerns (dependency, reliability, privacy, IP) and tips for teaching about AI. It advises instructors to put a syllabus statement in place and to state penalties, and lists CSULB-provided AI tools and the Turnitin detector with FERPA cautions.
documents.stance_why: The page promotes AI use in teaching and tells faculty to 'Provide a statement in your syllabus' but sets no rule for student use itself; it hands the decision to instructors, so delegates (not encourage, since it does not welcome student AI use in general).

units.why: Reasons that GenAI is or will be common in workplaces so 'giving students opportunities with relevant technologies ... prepares them for future jobs': professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools are or will be commonly used in workplaces.

units.why: Faculty are advised to 'Consider using AI to provide examples, analogies, and simple explanations'; instructor teaching use, P59.
units.anchor: Consider using AI to provide examples, analogies, and simple explanations.

units.why: Educators 'can use AI to clarify and expand on their feedback to students': instructor use for teaching work (feedback), P59.
units.anchor: Educators can use AI to clarify and expand on their feedback to students.

units.why: Faculty 'can encourage students to get immediate feedback from AI on their work': AI as a self-check and review aid for students, P14.
units.anchor: Faculty can encourage students to get immediate feedback from AI on their work.

units.why: AI-found culturally relevant examples 'should be fact-checked' against a trusted source: verify AI output, P31.
units.anchor: It should be fact-checked, by corroborating the example with a trusted source.

units.why: Lists AI as a 'personal tutor' with a suggested Socratic-tutor prompt, supporting student understanding rather than graded answers: P12.
units.anchor: Access a personal tutor.
units.policy: AI can serve as a personal tutor for students, for example with the prompt 'Act like a socratic tutor, who speaks in plain English.'

units.why: For revising a course, 'AI is great for brainstorming new ideas' (e.g. assessment ideas): instructor use for course design, P59.
units.anchor: AI is great for brainstorming new ideas.

units.why: Says AI 'can allow students with disabilities participate more fully', e.g. text read aloud; access and equity, P51.
units.anchor: can allow students with disabilities participate more fully

units.why: Warns that dependency on AI risks 'a decline in critical thinking and problem-solving abilities'; reliance undermines skill-building, P41.
units.anchor: The risks of students' dependency on AI include a decline in critical thinking

units.why: 'users will have to be aware of potential incorrect or made-up answers and examine the responses carefully': verify AI output, P31.
units.anchor: users will have to be aware of potential incorrect or made-up answers

units.why: Warns that users 'may unintentionally upload sensitive information' raising privacy, security and ethics questions: P50.
units.anchor: users may unintentionally upload sensitive information to the AI's database

units.why: Users should be 'mindful of the potential for intellectual property loss' as laws on AI content evolve: P52.
units.anchor: it's important to be mindful of the potential for intellectual property loss

units.why: Suggests instructors 'Teach students how AI is applied in a professional context' (company research, guest speakers): P44.
units.anchor: Teach students how AI is applied in a professional context:

units.why: Instructors should teach limitations such as 'AI can be inaccurate and even invent information', building verification habits: P31.
units.anchor: Teach students about the current limitations of AI tools:

units.why: Instructors should teach the societal implications of AI (misuse such as fake news and deepfakes): ethics and harms, P53.
units.anchor: Teach students about the societal implications of AI:

units.why: Under tips for faculty: 'Provide a statement in your syllabus': P09.
units.anchor: Provide a statement in your syllabus:

units.why: The syllabus statement should 'Be specific and let students know what class activities are permitted and not permitted': P09; this page is coded on its own, so the repeat of the syllabus-statements wording is kept.
units.anchor: Be specific and let students know what class activities are permitted

units.why: If prohibiting AI, instructors should 'clearly state the penalty for first-time offenders and those who repeatedly violate': stating penalties in advance, P37.
units.anchor: clearly state the penalty for first-time offenders and those who repeatedly violate

units.why: Offers custom ChatGPT tools built by ATS for faculty (learning objectives, quiz generator, rubric builder), accessed through the CSU ChatGPT account: university-provided sanctioned tools, P17.
units.anchor: tools developed by ATS Instructional Designers to support CSULB faculty

units.why: The CSULB Co-Research Agent is a sanctioned tool that guides students through topic refinement and searching while encouraging independent inquiry: P17.
units.anchor: helps students develop focused, academically rigorous research questions and literature review strategies

units.why: The Canvas Quiz Generator creates auto-graded quiz questions from instructor-provided material: instructors' AI use for teaching work, P59.
units.anchor: generates a variety of auto-graded quiz question types

units.why: The Canvas Rubric Builder helps faculty build rubrics: instructor use of AI for teaching work, P59.
units.anchor: helps faculty build rigorous, measurable rubrics aligned with assignment requirements

units.why: 'instructors can estimate the originality of work using Turnitin with AI Detection': a detection tool used to identify misuse, P40.
units.anchor: instructors can estimate the originality of work using Turnitin with AI Detection

units.why: Educators 'should not use other available AI detectors' because of FERPA; it protects student data and keeps to the vetted detector (P50; P39 does not fit because detectors are not rejected as unreliable).
units.anchor: educators should not use other available AI detectors

units.why: Instructors should first review what indicators mean and how false positives are handled 'Before challenging students': context-gathering before escalating, P57.
units.anchor: Before challenging students about the originality of their work, please review these links

units.why: Turnitin Draft Coach 'guides students in drafting assignments to properly cite references': a provided tool for students, P17.
units.anchor: guides students in drafting assignments to properly cite references

units.why: IgniteAI in Canvas Discussions summarizes themes and misconceptions for instructors: instructor use of AI in teaching work, P59.
units.anchor: summarizes key themes, questions, and helps to identify misconceptions and plan follow-up instruction

units.why: Microsoft Assignments helps faculty generate assignment instructions, rubrics and feedback: P59.
units.anchor: can help generate assignment instructions and rubrics and assist faculty in developing personalized feedback

units.why: Zoom AI Companion lecture summaries must be reviewed: 'After the lecture, review and edit the summary for accuracy' before posting; reviewing AI-made course materials, P48.
units.anchor: review and edit the summary for accuracy
units.policy: After the lecture, instructors review and edit the AI-generated summary for accuracy, add links or clarifications, and post it as a Canvas Announcement, Page, or Module item.

units.why: AI lecture summaries 'should supplement, not replace, student notes or approved note-taking accommodations', protecting accommodations: P51.
units.anchor: should supplement-not replace-student notes or approved note-taking accommodations

units.why: Offers customized AI training to departments and teams, plus workshops: supporting faculty in learning AI, P63.
units.anchor: Request customized training from Academic Technology Services for your department or team.

documents.title: Graduate Studies Generative AI Guidelines
documents.summary: Graduate Studies guidance for theses and dissertations that describes strengths and weaknesses of generative AI, privacy, environmental and citation concerns, and requires consulting professors and thesis advisors. It states it is not a policy and professors' rules take precedence.
documents.stance_why: The document says 'This document is not a CSULB or Graduate Studies policy' and that 'The professor's guidance, rules, and syllabus take precedence', and requires consulting the professor or advisor on whether AI is allowed; the decision is passed to instructors: delegates.

units.why: States it 'is not a CSULB or Graduate Studies policy' but supplementary guidance; sets the status of the framework: P56.
units.anchor: This document is not a CSULB or Graduate Studies policy.

units.why: For a particular assignment or class, graduate students 'must consult with their professor on whether the use of AI is allowed': the instructor decides, P04.
units.anchor: graduate students must consult with their professor on whether the use of AI is allowed
units.policy: For a particular assignment or class, graduate students must consult with their professor on whether the use of AI is allowed and the extent and capacity of that use.

units.why: 'The professor's guidance, rules, and syllabus take precedence over any guidance written here': the instructor's rule governs, P04.
units.anchor: The professor's guidance, rules, and syllabus take precedence over any guidance written here.

units.why: Defines generative AI as a prediction model crafting responses from user text and available data: P61.
units.anchor: generative AI uses a prediction model to craft customized responses

units.why: Says CSULB's Copilot is included in tuition and that the Division of IT suggests it is the safest free chatbot: a sanctioned university tool, P17.
units.anchor: CSULB's version of Copilot is included in students' tuition

units.why: Librarians recommend University databases because they provide 'broader, safer access to reliable information' than AI research tools; a source-reliability rule closest to P31.
units.anchor: CSULB Librarians recommend using the University's databases

units.why: Weakness list: AI provides true and false information and 'hallucinating' sources; warns that output may be wrong, P31.
units.anchor: Provides both true and false/inaccurate information

units.why: Weakness list: tools are 'Prone to bias' and answers 'retain, if not magnify, those biases': P53.
units.anchor: Prone to bias

units.why: Weakness: prompts and queries can inform responses to other users and become part of the database: privacy risk, P50.
units.anchor: Does not ensure that user queries are confidential

units.why: Students 'should take care in considering the level of privacy provided for the chatbot they are using': P50.
units.anchor: students should take care in considering the level of privacy provided

units.why: Students 'can adjust LLM settings to ensure confidentiality and privacy': P50.
units.anchor: Students can adjust LLM settings to ensure confidentiality and privacy.

units.why: 'Overreliance on GenAI to perform tasks may hinder one's skill development': outsourcing practice undermines learning, P41.
units.anchor: Overreliance on GenAI to perform tasks may hinder one's skill development

units.why: 'AI outputs cannot be judged well by those learning a field': novices cannot judge output, P42.
units.anchor: AI outputs cannot be judged well by those learning a field.

units.why: Weakness: 'Difficult to verify whether text is AI generated', with false positives; shows unreliability of detection, P39.
units.anchor: Difficult to verify whether text is AI generated

units.why: Describes AI data centers' electricity, water and materials use and emissions: environmental costs, P53.
units.anchor: AI data centers consume a great amount of electricity

units.why: Relying only on an AI literature summary is 'a lost opportunity of gaining the skills and experience of researching, synthesizing': skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: Solely using this information translates into a lost opportunity of gaining the skills

units.why: Students should use AI output as a first step, then check sources with Library resources and lateral reading: verification, P31.
units.anchor: use the AI tool's response as a first step
units.policy: Students use the AI tool's response as a first step, then use University Library resources to check the sources and corroborate via lateral reading.

units.why: Where the professor approved AI-generated results, 'it is important to properly cite this content': P24.
units.anchor: it is important to properly cite this content

units.why: Students follow their program's style guide (APA, Chicago, MLA) for citing AI; a citation-format rule, P25.
units.anchor: Students should follow the recommendations and citation format of whichever

units.why: Citation principles 'extend to figures, images, graphics, videos, and other multimedia generated using AI': P24.
units.anchor: These principles also extend to figures, images, graphics, videos, and other multimedia

units.why: In theses, reports, dissertations and comprehensive exams 'transparency of AI usage is of utmost importance': P24.
units.anchor: transparency of AI usage is of utmost importance

units.why: Students 'must consult their thesis advisors whether any usage of AI tools is allowed and appropriate': AI in theses, P62.
units.anchor: Students must consult their thesis advisors whether any usage of AI tools is allowed

units.why: If approved, students work with their advisor to document which tools were used and for what (brainstorming, outlining, researching, writing, editing): scholarship disclosure, P62.
units.anchor: the student should work with their advisor on ensuring full transparency of which AI tools
units.policy: If approved, the student works with their advisor on ensuring full transparency of which AI tools were used in their scholarly work and in which capacity.

units.why: Key takeaway: 'the purpose of graduate school is to learn; retain your agency': the student stays the primary thinker, P32.
units.anchor: retain your agency as a graduate scholar-researcher-

notes: Graduate Studies guidelines (csulb-gradstudies) cover CS MS students but are a university-level graduate document, not a computing-unit policy. Fabricating/falsifying data and faculty/staff nonconformity were coded UNCOVERED. Anchors were normalized to straight quotes and single spaces; type choices where two fit (e.g. P24 vs P25, P04 vs P01) are explained in each unit's why.
